lead: a first evening at a table where the others have twenty years, and by the coffee you have the shape of it — which two are finished, who is deferred to and never rung. nothing there has moved since.
sun: the introduction was made, the seat was yours, and the evening still happened from just outside the table. from inside twenty years, a table is a table. from where you were sitting it separated out into the two who will still be speaking in a decade, the one everybody defers to and nobody rings, and a marriage being carried by whichever of them is quieter.
moon: and then it closes over. what you took in that hour was never provisional and has never had a second pass, so eleven years on the version of each of them you work from was assembled before the plates were cleared. everyone else at that table has been amending since. you are still running the reading a stranger took in one sitting, and it is still the better one.
pull: you took the whole of them in an hour and have not looked since. from the same distance, in the same hour, they took one of you. neither reading has ever been reopened.
tension: say anything exact in the second year and it arrives from somebody who has been there five minutes, which converts an accurate sentence into a newcomer with opinions, so it stays in. meanwhile the reading they took across that first table — reserved, watchful, hard to place — has the same staying power yours does, and eleven years of turning up has not amended a word of it.
cost: an hour among people who owe you nothing gives you the true structure of them, which nobody who grew up inside that structure will ever hold. all of them are kept at the size they were that night. whoever improved afterwards improved outside your reading, and at that table you are still introduced as the one who came in late.

lead: the committee everybody privately called theatre was wound up inside a year of your appointment. you had said as much once, mildly, at a table where you were still the newest person. nothing is said mildly from that chair.
sun: they promoted the outside view. what the place wanted was somebody who could see it, and the only people who can see it are the ones who were never entirely in the room — so the sorting came up the building with you: which of the two divisions is carrying the thing, which arrangement is a courtesy nobody has withdrawn, which senior pair stopped agreeing in private some while ago.
moon: a carved seat does not permit a passing remark. the bearing that got you here, level and unflinching when a thing lands, is read as deliberation, so an observation you turned over on a wednesday leaves you as the settled view of a body older than everyone in it. nobody asks the chair whether it was thinking aloud.
pull: a sorting you did in your own head at the weekend leaves that seat as policy. the place has come apart twice along lines you believed you were only describing.
tension: there is no register available to you between silence and ruling. a doubt spoken in a corridor turns up minuted in a document you never see, so people stop bringing you the ordinary state of things and start bringing the version that survives being decided about. the institution that raised you for seeing it clearly has, since about your second year, been arranging what you see.
cost: a place cannot name its own ornament, and you can, from a seat with the standing to act on it — which is why the record holds two decades it might not have had. what you name does not come apart slowly and does not come apart later. the people who ran those parts can quote the sentence and say who was sitting in the chair.

lead: a half-step off a group you belong to cannot be taken quietly here. The Mane comes at one size, the size a doorway registers, so the gap between you and them is the most legible thing in the hall.
sun: the seat had your name on it and you are in the photographs, and none of it has ever put you inside the day the way the others are. from where you stand the hall separates out: the couple everyone treats as the centre and is not, the two who came separately and will leave together, the ones here out of duty to somebody who died. you had all of it before the speeches.
moon: nothing about it happens discreetly. the display arrives at one size, set before you had a view on the matter, so a position you never chose goes out at the width of everything else about you, from the moment you come through the door. people who cannot see the hall as you see it can see, at fifty feet, that you are seeing it. that is what registers.
pull: you did not choose the half-step and cannot make it smaller. what you are known for is a position — the one membership in that group anybody has an opinion about.
tension: aloof arrives early and stays, and the kind version is that you were always a bit apart. turning up harder answers neither, because arriving first and leaving last is visible at exactly the same width and lands as somebody making a case for themselves. so a group with no argument about whether you are one of theirs keeps an open question about you anyway, raised at every gathering by people who mean well.
cost: somebody's mother takes you aside at each of these and asks what you make of the new one, and what you tell her is worth more than any other answer in the hall, and it holds up. an evening in there with nothing to see is not something you have had. their account of you is a person standing slightly outside their happiest days, at that width, in every photograph.

lead: you were done with it inside a season, nothing left over, no lapsed version, nothing kept for the anniversaries. because it was you who went, what you had said about the place for years landed as a verdict.
sun: thirty years of turning up, and everyone there knew you were not quite one of them, which is why your going could not be a private matter. a member who was always slightly outside is the member whose departure gets read for information. they spent the year afterwards going over what you had seen, and some of them found it, and the part they found was true.
moon: the going had no gradient. no thinning year, no coming to the summer thing, no half of the tie kept for the ones you liked — the whole of it was over by spring, and none of the belonging is in you now. what did not end is what you owe them. you pay what you said you would pay, you are at the hospital, you are at the funerals.
pull: the leaving was total and every duty survived it intact. what they have now is somebody who meets each obligation to them and is not in any of it at all.
tension: a group has arrangements for drifting off — a quiet year, a lapsed subscription, a person who is just busy — and nothing at all for somebody who is finished. so the exit is read as the sentence you never said, and the ones who left afterwards cite you. settling every account makes it worse: a person who is gone and still pays looks like a person making a point, and the point they read is about them.
cost: nobody is dropped when you go and nothing is left for other people to clear up; the ending is total and every account in it is square. what you cannot do is leave quietly. the reading of that place you spent thirty years assembling walked out of the door with you, in a form nobody in there can check, and it is still working on them.
